name: targets
about: Where sandboxes can run: isolation in members' words (tier, tierMeans, tierRank), network control, state.

benefits: A separate kernel in user space (gVisor): the host kernel's attack surface is cut
Network allow list enforced on the host
Fastest cold start of SandHold's engines (about <span>); warm about <span>
limits: Allow list only: no per-request HTTP rules or credential injection
Some system calls are unsupported or slower (heavy file and network I/O)
about.title: SandHold Sealed

targets.name: gvisor
targets.tierMeans: its own kernel in user space

benefits: Its own guest kernel in a hardware-virtualised VM (Kata Containers): the strongest separation
Network allow list enforced on the host
Warm start about <span> from the node's pool
limits: Allow list only: no per-request HTTP rules or credential injection
Cold start about <span>; uses more memory per sandbox
about.title: SandHold Vault

targets.name: kata
targets.tierMeans: its own kernel in a virtual machine

benefits: Hardened container: no capabilities, syscall filter, non-root user, read-only /usr
Full network control: allow list, per-request HTTP rules and credentials injected on the wire
Warm start about <span> from the node's pool
limits: Cold start about <span> (the egress proxy starts with it)
about.title: SandHold Shielded

targets.name: runc
targets.tierMeans: a hardened container on the host's kernel
